## Part 2: Ranking

This file picks up where `01_key_frame_and_criteria.Rmd` left off. It reads
`final_key_df.csv` and `treated61-2.csv` fresh from disk, so it can be run
on its own any time after Part 1 has been run at least once — it does not
need Part 1's R session to still be open.

```{r load_inputs}

library(dplyr)

# ---- Load inputs saved by 01_key_frame_and_criteria.Rmd ----
final_key_df <- read.csv("final_key_df.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(CVEGEO = formatC(CVEGEO, width = 5, format = "d", flag = "0"))

treated <- read.csv("treated61-2.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(CVEGEO = formatC(CVEGEO, width = 5, format = "d", flag = "0"))

nrow(final_key_df)   # expect 2478
nrow(treated)         # expect 61

```

```{r build_composite}

# ---- Z-score each criteria variable ----
# scale() computes mean/sd using only non-missing values, and leaves NA as NA
# — important, since n_inseguro_popw has missing municipalities (not sampled in 2025)
composite_index <- final_key_df %>%
  mutate(
    z_homicidios = as.numeric(scale(homicidios_total)),
    z_robos      = as.numeric(scale(robos_total)),
    z_inseguro   = as.numeric(scale(n_inseguro_popw))   # will have NAs where not sampled
  )

# ---- Confirm scaling worked as expected ----
mean(composite_index$z_homicidios, na.rm = TRUE)   # expect ~0
sd(composite_index$z_homicidios, na.rm = TRUE)      # expect ~1
mean(composite_index$z_robos, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(composite_index$z_robos, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(composite_index$z_inseguro, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(composite_index$z_inseguro, na.rm = TRUE)

# ---- Flag non-sampled municipalities BEFORE filling ----
composite_index <- composite_index %>%
  mutate(
    non_sampled_ensu = if_else(is.na(z_inseguro), 1, 0)
  )

# ---- Audit the flag before filling ----
sum(composite_index$non_sampled_ensu)                  # how many municipalities weren't sampled
mean(composite_index$non_sampled_ensu)                 # what share of all municipalities
sum(is.na(composite_index$z_inseguro))                 # should match sum(non_sampled_ensu)

# ---- Now fill missing z_inseguro with 0 ----
composite_index <- composite_index %>%
  mutate(
    z_inseguro = if_else(is.na(z_inseguro), 0, z_inseguro)
  )

# ---- Confirm no NAs remain in any z-score column ----
sum(is.na(composite_index$z_homicidios))
sum(is.na(composite_index$z_robos))
sum(is.na(composite_index$z_inseguro))                 # should now be 0

# ---- Build the equal-weight composite ----
composite_index <- composite_index %>%
  mutate(
    composite_equal = (z_homicidios + z_robos + z_inseguro) / 3
  )

# ---- Sanity extremes ----
composite_index %>% arrange(desc(composite_equal)) %>% head(5) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, homicidios_total, robos_total, n_inseguro_popw, composite_equal)
composite_index %>% arrange(composite_equal) %>% head(5) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, homicidios_total, robos_total, n_inseguro_popw, composite_equal)

# ---- Spot check: does a non_sampled row actually have z_inseguro == 0? ----
composite_index %>% filter(non_sampled_ensu == 1) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, z_inseguro) %>% head()

```

```{r rank_composite}

# ---- Produce ranks: rank 1 = worst (highest composite value) ----
composite_index <- composite_index %>%
  mutate(
    rank_composite_equal = min_rank(desc(composite_equal))
  ) %>%
  arrange(rank_composite_equal)   # order the whole table by rank

# ---- Confirm rank 1 = worst ----
head(composite_index, 1) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, homicidios_total, robos_total, n_inseguro_popw, composite_equal, rank_composite_equal)

# This should be the SAME municipality you saw at the top of your
# arrange(desc(composite_equal)) sanity check above — if not, something's off

# ---- Confirm the bottom of the ranking looks "best" (lowest composite) ----
tail(composite_index, 1) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, homicidios_total, robos_total, n_inseguro_popw, composite_equal, rank_composite_equal)

# ---- Explicit assertion: rank 1 really is the max composite value ----
stopifnot(
  composite_index$CVEGEO[composite_index$rank_composite_equal == 1] ==
  composite_index$CVEGEO[which.max(composite_index$composite_equal)]
)

# ---- Eyeball top-ranked municipalities ----
top_ranked <- head(composite_index, 61)
top_ranked %>% select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, composite_equal, rank_composite_equal)

```

```{r join_treated}

# ---- Join treated status onto the ranked composite ----
composite_index <- composite_index %>%
  left_join(
    treated %>% select(CVEGEO, gov_inclusion_code),
    by = "CVEGEO"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_treated = if_else(!is.na(gov_inclusion_code), 1, 0)
  )

# ---- Audit ----
sum(composite_index$is_treated)          # should be 61
table(composite_index$gov_inclusion_code, useNA = "ifany")

# ---- How many treated municipalities fall in the worst-ranked group? ----
composite_index %>%
  filter(rank_composite_equal <= 61) %>%
  summarise(n_treated_in_top = sum(is_treated))

# ---- Break that down by criteria-based vs strategic ----
composite_index %>%
  filter(rank_composite_equal <= 61) %>%
  count(gov_inclusion_code)

# ---- Which treated municipalities did NOT make the worst-ranked cut? ----
composite_index %>%
  filter(is_treated == 1, rank_composite_equal > 61) %>%
  select(CVEGEO, NOMGEO, gov_inclusion_code, composite_equal, rank_composite_equal) %>%
  arrange(rank_composite_equal)

```

```{r save_output}

# ---- Save, already in rank order ----
write.csv(composite_index, "composite_index.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
